title: Algebraic inverse Lefschetz operators
as_he_states: The correspondence ring should contain inverses of the complementary-degree Lefschetz isomorphisms, equivalently normalized lowering and the primitive projectors; the letter calls this C.
plausible_today: For every smooth projective X over a field with a specified Weil cohomology, each inverse to L^(n−i) is induced by a rational algebraic correspondence: modern standard conjecture B. Hard Lefschetz and algebraicity are separate.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 Proposition2.9 gives equivalences; Theorem2.13 gives product/hyperplane reductions. Deligne1980 Theorem4.1.1 proves rational ell-adic hard Lefschetz, not B. Ancona et al.2025 prove specified LSV/Lagrangian cases, not the universal claim.
why_open: The obstruction is existence of algebraic correspondences. No source says the general conjecture was dropped; it remains an active problem.
worth: Worth a focused historical/formal reconstruction, while a general proof is far beyond a short research run.

title: Definition and normalization of the universal integral model
as_he_states: The definition numbered6.5 is unfinished; the exterior model is said to work over Z and to give a universal algebra.
plausible_today: A valid normalized integral string algebra is ∏ Mat_(n−i+1)(Z); its relation to the literal ordinary exterior-contraction order must be specified rather than assumed.
state_of_art: The factorial and contraction counterchecks refute the literal model. The earlier notes’ replacement is proved in proof_checks§3 with exact certificates. Kleiman1968 supplies the formal rational/cohomological framework, not an identification of these integral orders.
why_open: The pages leave the normalization incomplete and contain incompatible claims; no documentary reason for abandonment is known.
worth: Worth a bounded editorial task to compare lattices and operator conventions, with no claim that the repaired model is his unwritten definition.

title: Uniqueness when only the raising operator is specified
as_he_states: Could there be at most one map Φ→E taking the universal L to L without a prescribed grading? He answers Non on scan17.
plausible_today: Uniqueness can hold with the appropriate prescribed graded projectors; it is false without them, already for n=1.
state_of_art: Source own negative answer, independently certified by Ad(1+tL) on Mat₂(Z)×Z. Kleiman’s graded formalism is consistent with the qualified uniqueness.
why_open: Resolved negatively on the same page, not a surviving open conjecture.
worth: Worth recording the short counterexample in a companion, not launching a separate attempt to prove the rejected claim.

title: Recovering degree and primitive projectors inside a correspondence ring
as_he_states: Give an existence/uniqueness induction recovering π_i and the elementary primitive projectors from homogeneous inverse maps.
plausible_today: Under finite grading and two-sided inverse identities, use two-sided truncated blocks T_kL^(n−k)T_k and T_kw_kT_k, followed by supported primitive differences.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 Lemma3.15 and Proposition2.9 give the formal theorem. This run proves the explicit repaired induction and refutes the one-sided cutoff on H*(P²).
why_open: The written proof has an off-by-one terminal step and a missing target cutoff. Neither is a reason to regard the theorem itself as false.
worth: Worth immediate editorial repair with the source formulas and reconstructed proof displayed separately.

title: Characterizing Lefschetz elements by top powers
as_he_states: Can nonvanishing or being a basis of E^(2n) for L^n characterize Lefschetz elements?
plausible_today: Such a criterion needs additional control of all middle-degree maps; it fails even in the displayed six-dimensional commutative graded algebra.
state_of_art: The manuscript’s own presentation has ranks1,2,2,1; L is Lefschetz while L′ has rank-one middle map and the same nonzero cube. Exact matrices certify every relation.
why_open: The proposed converse is rejected on scan22 by his own example.
worth: Worth retaining as a clean warning against endpoint-only tests; additional classification is a new task.

title: Rational dependence of lowering on the raising operator
as_he_states: The scratch formula is Λ=Ω(L)Δ(L)^(−N), with Ω,Δ,N undefined.
plausible_today: On a specified finite free graded module, inverse matrices depend regularly after inverting determinants of all relevant Lefschetz blocks; a universal expression needs an explicit parameter algebra and normalization.
state_of_art: Formal inverse/characteristic-polynomial methods appear in Kleiman1968. No exact theorem matching the undefined scratch expression was identified in title, formula or backward-reference searches.
why_open: The source is unfinished; no evidence establishes why it was not pursued.
worth: Worth a small reconstruction only after the parameter space and coefficient ring have been fixed from the scans.

title: Infinite orbits in the four-form Hodge-algebra model
as_he_states: The orbits of ξ and φ̌ under u should be infinite when dimV≥4, or perhaps6.
plausible_today: For the explicitly reconstructed operator U=(Λ²φ♯)Q♭, dimension6 suffices with Q nondegenerate, Q(ξ,ξ)=1 and φ nondegenerate; the sharp dimension4 threshold and the literal tensor convention remain separate.
state_of_art: The earlier-run rational six-dimensional example is independently rechecked in the full15×15 space. Exact literature searches found no matched published resolution. Positivity/geometric realization are not asserted.
why_open: The author explicitly doubts the threshold and leaves u’s tensor normalization compressed; those are genuine limits on identification.
worth: Worth a short convention-and-threshold task after an ink check; the existing dimension6 certificate prevents needless rediscovery.

title: Unbounded cyclic spans of those orbits
as_he_states: The orbit spans should have unbounded dimension as dimV grows.
plausible_today: For the earlier normalized U, the proposed family has cyclic span dimension at least m in dimV=4m, with a normalized nondegenerate four-form model.
state_of_art: The supplied earlier-run family is checked by a general Vandermonde/open-condition argument and exact m=2,3,4 cases. No exact publication of the family was identified.
why_open: No source records why the manuscript claim was left unproved; the normalization remains the decisive interpretation issue.
worth: Worth including the already available proof under its explicit convention, with further geometric constraints reserved for another task.

title: Associativity and norm constraints in Hodge-algebra data
as_he_states: He writes a boxed associativity condition, a four-form reformulation, an isotropic-line example and the claim that a suitable norm-one ξ yields any φ up to scalar.
plausible_today: Keep associativity separate from nondegeneracy. For the final norm-one choice require the inverse image of φ to have nonzero norm in the appropriate square class.
state_of_art: Direct algebra verifies the associativity criterion, Poincaré/Lefschetz conditions and isotropic example. The norm-one assertion is not valid over an arbitrary field without qualifications. No exact later classification was identified.
why_open: The norm qualification is absent; the parameter-space classification is an earlier-run research suggestion, not a stated theorem of his.
worth: Worth a narrowly labelled editorial clarification; moduli or geometric realization should be a separate research project.

title: Discriminant pairing versus local étale duality
as_he_states: The notes ask whether exceptional-lattice self-duality equals the quotient pairing coming from local cohomological duality; his published continuation explicitly leaves this verification undone.
plausible_today: For the precise complete normal local surface setup, identify NS(U)_n and Pic(U)^0[n] as exact annihilators and compare the quotient pairing with xᵀQ⁻¹y, including twists and sign conventions.
state_of_art: BrauerIII§8.4pp148–151 sets up the problem; Remark8.5p151 admits the missing check. Suzuki2024 Proposition11.10 gives an explicit analogous intersection/duality compatibility in a mixed-characteristic p-primary setting; its hypotheses are not the same as the original equal-characteristic char0 statement.
why_open: The published text identifies the check and says it was not done, while expecting no difficulty. This documents a historical proof gap, not by itself a presently open theorem.
worth: Worth a focused comparison of the exact pairings and later proofs; its statement is concrete and directly connected to local Picard/Brauer theory.

title: Characteristic and residue-field extensions of local Picard–Brauer duality
as_he_states: The published continuation says characteristic0 enters through local duality, expects removal of that restriction, and asks about non-algebraically-closed residue fields such as finite fields.
plausible_today: Separate prime-to-characteristic étale duality from p-primary duality, and retain complete normal two-dimensional local hypotheses; finite/perfect residue fields require Galois or algebraic-group structure.
state_of_art: BrauerIII Remark8.5 states the old purity obstacle. Suzuki2024 develops mixed-characteristic perfect-residue-field Picard–Brauer duality, Theorem1.6 and §11, building on Saito1986/1987. Exact comparison with the old pairings is a further task.
why_open: The reason given in1968 is missing cohomological purity in regular dimension2; the modern arithmetic setting has additional p-primary structures.
worth: Worth a literature-matching task, not a blanket claim that the old statement is either wholly open or wholly solved.

title: Hyperplane operator formulary and its boundaries
as_he_states: Derive the restriction/Gysin/primitive and lowering formulas needed to transfer algebraicity along a smooth hyperplane.
plausible_today: Use finite Lefschetz strings with the extra primitive middle summand on Y; all formulas must respect endpoint supports and the strict inequality in projector transfer.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Proposition2.12 and Theorem2.13 establish the formal reductions. This run checks all displayed compressed identities and demonstrates the false non-strict boundary extension.
why_open: The pages revise symbols and endpoints repeatedly; this is a draft proof problem, not an unresolved geometric theorem once hypotheses are fixed.
worth: Worth a companion formulary with explicit domains and endpoint projectors.

title: Strong from weak Lefschetz through product-cycle conditions
as_he_states: He proposes equivalent conditions using B(Y) together with critical algebraic-cycle Lefschetz conditions on X×X or X×Y, and then flags.
plausible_today: The product and universal quantifiers must be retained: A(k) over all varieties is equivalent to B(k), whereas A(X) for one variety does not imply B(X) by this argument.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem2.13 and3.16 are the exact developed results. No missing inverse cycle is produced without the product hypothesis.
why_open: The formal reduction was developed; the cycle existence input remains conjectural generally.
worth: Worth a precise dependency diagram in the future companion, with no new proof program launched here.

title: The A′ and A″ critical weak variants
as_he_states: He asserts that two critical weak lifting conditions on successive products imply the full Lefschetz cycle relation.
plausible_today: A consistent cohomological-degree convention should recover a theorem of the product/hyperplane type; the current H^i versus2i and j/i expressions cannot all be used literally.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem2.13 is the precise nearby theorem. This run does not claim that it decides the ambiguous draft letters or inequalities.
why_open: The difficulty here is identifying a coherent source statement, rather than a new obstacle in the published formal proof.
worth: Worth an ink-first transcription task followed by exact matching to the published theorem.

title: Independence of the chosen cohomology theory
as_he_states: He retracts the hasty positive-characteristic assertion that the stated cycle conditions are independent of ell or the Weil cohomology.
plausible_today: Under numerical=homological equivalence and the relevant standard/positivity hypotheses, the correspondence category and conditions admit the desired independence; unconditional universality is stronger.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem3.16 gives conditional independence. Jannsen1992 proves semisimplicity for numerical motives and a conditional nilpotent kernel, not the full homological conclusion.
why_open: The letter itself identifies lack of a proof in characteristicp; no later numerical theorem removes every condition.
worth: Worth a historical hypothesis audit; a general independence proof is not a short task.

title: Polarization independence in positive characteristic
as_he_states: If Coates cannot prove independence of A and C from ξ in characteristicp, the possible dependence should be pointed out.
plausible_today: Modern inverse-Lefschetz B is polarization independent under its formal hypotheses; an independently stated cycle condition A must be matched to its exact definition and any index assumption.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Proposition2.10 proves the relevant inverse-Lefschetz polarization independence. The draft’s undefined B/D letters are not translated by letter alone.
why_open: This is a specific doubt in the letter, later resolved in the formal B setting; the page does not supply definitions for every letter.
worth: Worth a small exact-notation concordance, not a universal equivalence assertion.

title: Rational characteristic polynomials in positive characteristic
as_he_states: He hopes the characteristic0 simplification from an algebraic isomorphism to its inverse could also be obtained in arbitrary characteristic.
plausible_today: Require rational characteristic polynomials of the relevant algebraic endomorphisms, or a precise theorem guaranteeing them in the chosen cohomology; then Cayley–Hamilton gives the inverse.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Propositions2.7 and2.9 provide the conditional result. Katz–Messing1974Theorem2(1)–(2),pp76–77, directly read with proof, gives finite-field characteristic-polynomial integrality for integral correspondences and rational Künneth projectors. It does not establish all-field homological= numerical equivalence.
why_open: The draft correctly isolates the coefficient issue; later finite-field results cover a specified setting.
worth: Worth matching the exact finite-field theorem and its descent hypotheses before broadening the letter’s assertion.

title: Positivity and semisimple correspondence algebras
as_he_states: He asks that C(X) plus the index relation on X×X imply semisimplicity of correspondence classes.
plausible_today: For the algebraic adjoint involution and a positive rational trace form, prove finite-dimensionality and kill the radical by its trace norm.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem3.12/Lemma3.13 establish it; this run independently supplies the radical and rational Gram-matrix arguments. Jannsen1992 concerns numerical motives separately.
why_open: The requested formal result was developed. The geometric positivity assumptions remain nontrivial in positive characteristic.
worth: Worth a concise proof in the companion with the conditional assumptions visible.

title: Algebraic left and right inverses
as_he_states: He expects an algebraic monomorphism to have an algebraic left inverse, and dually a right inverse for an epimorphism, apparently needing the index relation.
plausible_today: Assume algebraic adjoints and positivity in the correspondence setting containing both source and target; then (u*u)^−1u* supplies the left inverse.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem3.14 develops the result. Semisimplicity of a single unrelated endomorphism algebra alone does not control all off-diagonal correspondences.
why_open: The source already distinguishes isomorphisms from injections; the latter need stronger ambient data.
worth: Worth a categorical hypothesis clarification and the explicit splitting formula.

title: Deriving the Weil bounds from cycle conjectures
as_he_states: He requests an extra paragraph deducing the Weil conjectures from draft C and A.
plausible_today: State the precise positivity-bearing package, such as algebraic Lefschetz operators plus I(X×X), rather than relying on undefined letters.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem4.7 develops the conditional argument. Deligne’s later proof of Weil bounds does not prove the whole standard-conjecture package.
why_open: The program was developed conditionally and later the bounds were proved by a different method; no source supports identifying the two achievements.
worth: Worth a clear logical-history paragraph; no new general Weil proof is needed.

title: One-cycles on threefolds and the dimension-five critical case
as_he_states: He says the main difficulty already arises for1-cycles on threefolds, and the first critical A case in characteristic0 is dimension5, notably X×Y for a threefold and hyperplane surface.
plausible_today: Retain rational coefficients and the distinction between cycle-Lefschetz A and inverse-correspondence B; the product condition of dimension5 would provide B for the threefold.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968Theorem2.13 gives this implication; low-degree algebraicity via Picard/Albanese is in2A9–2A10. Modern special cases do not settle all smooth projective threefolds.
why_open: The manuscript identifies the first nontrivial codimension beyond divisors; the general algebraic-cycle existence remains difficult.
worth: Worth a targeted known-case inventory, not a claim that low-dimensional hard Lefschetz settles the algebraic inverse.

title: A singular-variety reformulation after the hypersurface obstruction
as_he_states: After Serre’s simply-connectedness objection to the smooth-hypersurface reduction, he says singular hypersurfaces and a reformulation of standard conjectures for singular varieties would be needed.

state_of_art: SGA1X3.4 and3.8–3.9 provide the birational/specialization framework underlying the obstruction. No unique singular-variety conjecture is formulated on the page.
why_open: The smooth reduction is explicitly abandoned because it would force trivial fundamental group; the singular replacement is only a program.
worth: Worth an editorial history note; choosing a modern singular theory is a separate research task.
